Subject: Reliability SLO follow-up & next tests

Thanks again for taking the call today — really helpful to understand NimbusAI's production constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs:
- High availability across US regions (target: 99.99% for inference endpoint)
- Predictable rate limits for bursty batch scoring (peaks up to 5k rps for short windows)
- Clear error budget and failover behavior for multi-region outages
- Auditability: per-request traces, request/response TTLs, and retention controls

What Redwood can provide (high level):
- Baseline SLO: 99.95% global uptime with options to upgrade to SLA-backed 99.99% on Dedicated capacity
- Configurable rate-limit tiers and token-based concurrency controls; per-route QPS caps and burst windows
- Automatic cross-region failover with warm-standby model variants and graceful degradation to lower-cost quantized variants
- Audit logs + KV prefix caching to reduce per-token cost for repeat requests

Proposed next tests (I'll coordinate):
1) SLO/uptime baseline: we run a 48h synthetic traffic test from your staging region vs a hyperscaler endpoint (you provide the test harness or we can run with k6)
2) Rate-limit shock test: simulate 5k rps sustained for 2 minutes to validate throttling behavior and tail latency
3) Failover exercise: simulate an AZ+region failure and observe traffic shift and 99th/99.9th percentile latencies
4) Error budget telemetry: validate alerts and breakdowns when error budget usage exceeds thresholds

Attachments: I'll follow up with a short SLO comparison spreadsheet and a one-pager on our reliability architecture.

Next steps:
- Sarah / Tom: confirm which tests you want Redwood to run vs run yourselves (and preferred windows)
- Nimbus: share staging endpoint and any rate-limit test scripts
- Redwood: deliver SLO comparison spreadsheet + pre-test checklist by EOD tomorrow

Thanks — looking forward to running these with you.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — answering inline below and attaching the comparison deck + spreadsheet (slo_comparison.xlsx, redwood-reliability.pdf).

On costs & upgrade path:
- SLA-backed 99.99% requires Dedicated reserved capacity (1 month minimum), volume-based pricing; rough ballpark: 30% premium over hosted at equivalent QPS. I can get a formal quote once we size the reservation.

On tail latency during bursts:
- Guarantee depends on model profile and allocated GPU pool. For typical decoder models at <2k seq length we regularly achieve sub-200ms p99 on Dedicated pools sized for burst headroom. Hosted plans have higher variability; we recommend Dedicated for strict p99 targets. We'll include model-size-specific estimates in the spreadsheet.

On error budget & alerts:
- Yes: per-route error budget panels are available in Redwood Console; we can emit alerts to PagerDuty, Slack, and webhook endpoints. Error budget windows and thresholds are configurable per-service.

On fallback behavior when primary region saturates or loses capacity:
- Smart routing will route to warm-standby clusters in another region. Options:
  * Fail-open to a quantized/cheaper variant (lower quality) to keep latency and availability for critical requests
  * Queue requests briefly while spinning extra capacity (if burst latency SLO permits)
  * Circuit-break (reject) with graceful error code plus cached prefix responses for repeat queries

Attachments included: slo_comparison.xlsx (tabbed with uptime/rate-limit comparisons vs AWS/GC/Redwood hosted+dedicated) and redwood-reliability.pdf (1-pager on failover and warm-standby design).

Proposed immediate plan: we will run tests 1 (48h synthetic) and 2 (rate shock) on Wed 2026-03-18 morning PT as you suggested. Please reply with staging endpoints and any test scripts by EOD Monday so we can provision Dedicated test capacity if needed.

Thanks — Ben
